---
title: "Business Critical analysis"
description: "The steps to follow when an impact dimension scores Level 4."
---

NHSBSA defines Business Critical analysis as follows:

> "Business Critical Analysis informs major policy, funding, statutory, regulatory or
> customer-impacting decisions. The analysis is essential to the achievement of business plan
> actions and priorities. Errors could lead to significant patient or user impacts or serious
> financial, legal, reputational damages or penalties"

The [Analytical Assurance Decision Tool spreadsheet]({{< var decision-tool >}}) decides whether
work is Business Critical: a Level 4 score on any one of its six impact dimensions. Opening it needs an NHSBSA account with access to the Analytical Quality
and Assurance site. Business Critical work is assured at Level 4 BCA and goes on the Business
Critical register. Start at step 1.

## Steps by phase

| Step | Phase | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Decide whether it is Business Critical](#step-1-decide-at-scoping-whether-it-is-business-critical) | Phase 1 | The Business Critical answer, recorded yes or no |
| [2. Name who is accountable](#step-2-name-who-is-accountable) | Phase 1 | A named Analysis Senior Responsible Officer |
| [3. Read the assurance level](#step-3-read-the-assurance-level) | Phase 1 | The likelihood scored, and the tool complete |
| [4. Get it on the register and arrange external assurance](#step-4-get-it-on-the-register) | Phase 1 | The register entry, and the external assurer arranged |
| [5. Do the work to Level 4 BCA](#step-5-do-the-work-to-the-enhanced-standard) | Phases 1 to 4 | The eleven documents of the stack, each in the phase the picture gives |
| [6. Say what is uncertain](#step-6-say-what-is-uncertain) | Phase 3 | The uncertainty documented and quantified |
| [7. Get sign-off, then publish what was checked](#step-7-publish-what-was-checked) | Phase 4 | The sign-off, and the quality assurance statement published with the output |
| [8. Set a review date and approve any new use](#step-8-keep-it-true-after-first-use) | Phase 5 | A review date, and approval of any new use |
| [9. Review the work and revalidate the designation](#step-9-review-and-revalidate-the-designation) | Phase 5 | The designation revalidated |

## Step 1. Decide at scoping whether it is Business Critical {#step-1-decide-at-scoping-whether-it-is-business-critical}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/bca-determination.qmd >}}

## Step 2. Name who is accountable {#step-2-name-who-is-accountable}

The commissioner names an Analysis Senior Responsible Officer at scoping, with the Analytical
Quality and Assurance Lead.

- They must be senior enough to carry the risks across the lifecycle.
- They approve the work as fit for purpose before it is used.
- The commissioner may take the role.

::: {.nhsuk-inset-text}
More detail: [the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer role](/guidance/06-roles/analysis-senior-responsible-officer.qmd).
:::

## Step 3. Read the assurance level {#step-3-read-the-assurance-level}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/bca-assurance-level.qmd >}}

## Step 4. Get it on the register and arrange external assurance {#step-4-get-it-on-the-register}

Log the work with the Data Science, Statistics and AI team, which holds the Business Critical
register. Do this whether or not the work is a model. The entry is added to NHSBSA's public
register of Business Critical analyses, and NHSBSA reports on that work each year to the Data,
Analytics and AI Governance Council, to the Department of Health and Social Care and in its annual
report. See [who to ask](/guidance/09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd)
for how to reach the team.

At the same time, arrange an independent external assurer for the additional scrutiny and testing
that Level 4 BCA asks for.

Add each part of the entry when it exists:

- at scoping, the accountable officer, who is the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, and the intended use
- as they are produced, the user documentation and the guidance on quality assurance
- at sign-off, the officer's confirmation that the work is suitable for its intended use

## Step 5. Do the work to Level 4 BCA {#step-5-do-the-work-to-the-enhanced-standard}

Do everything Level 3 Comprehensive requires. Follow the Level 3 checks in
[what your level requires](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#what-each-phase-requires).

Level 4 BCA adds these checks:

- formal audits
- external review
- additional scrutiny of the documentation
- scrutiny of the structural and conceptual assumptions
- additional scenario testing

Check that everyone using and assuring the work has the skills and knowledge for it. Where they do
not, arrange specialist induction or training.

### The documentation stack

Complete the eleven documents below, generally in the order shown. Update an earlier document when a
review shows it needs changing. For an analysis that already exists, review what is there, find the
gaps and fill them first.

The picture shows who owns each document and the phase it belongs to. The table links each template.
Opening them needs an NHSBSA account with access to the Analytical Quality and Assurance site.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-documents-by-role-and-phase.qmd >}}

| No. | Document |
|-----|------------------------------------------|
| 1 | Analytical plan. [Analysis plan template]({{< var template-analysis-plan >}}) |
| 2 | Scope. [Scope template]({{< var template-scope >}}) |
| 3 | [Analytical Assurance Decision Tool spreadsheet]({{< var decision-tool >}}) |
| 4 | Specification. [Specification template]({{< var template-specification >}}) |
| 5 | Quality assurance plan. [Quality assurance plan template]({{< var template-qa-plan >}}) |
| 6 | Quality assurance appraisal, basic information |
| 7 | The analysis or model itself, which has no template |
| 8 | Technical guide. [Technical guide template]({{< var template-technical-guide >}}) |
| 9 | User guide. [User guide template]({{< var template-user-guide >}}) |
| 10 | Quality assurance appraisal, assurance review |
| 11 | Quality assurance sign-off |

: The eleven Business Critical documents, in order, with their templates

For document 7, use the Model Guidance Document and the
[checklist for building an analytical solution]({{< var template-building-checklist >}}).

Three more templates support the stack: [document control and information governance]({{< var template-document-control >}}),
[knowledge management]({{< var template-knowledge-management >}}) and
[version control]({{< var template-version-control >}}). All three are in the
[Analytical Quality Assurance Templates folder]({{< var templates-folder >}}). NHSBSA also lists a
risk log and an assumptions log among its templates.

- Give each action in the quality assurance plan and the assurance review a priority of Must, Should or Could.
- Hold the documentation centrally with the Analytical Quality and Assurance function, and send it each new production version of a model.
- Name each file with the document type first, for example `User_Guide_AnalysisName`.

[What each document holds, and how the stack is scored and held](../09-resources/r2-templates-and-documents.qmd#the-business-critical-documentation-stack) is in Resources.

## Step 6. Say what is uncertain {#step-6-say-what-is-uncertain}

Document the uncertainty. Quantify it wherever the method allows, as at Level 3.

Write down any assumption that would change the answer if it were wrong.

::: {.nhsuk-inset-text}
More detail: [what uncertainty is, how to manage it and how to write it up](/guidance/09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd).
:::

## Step 7. Get sign-off, then publish what was checked {#step-7-publish-what-was-checked}

Get sign-off from the Lead Assurer, then from the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. Your
commissioner then signs it off for release. Update the Business Critical register entry when the
work is signed off.

Then publish the quality assurance statement with the output. From Level 3, it carries what
[Phase 4](/guidance/04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) lists. At Level 4 BCA it also carries:

- the Business Critical register reference
- the Lead Assurer, named, from outside the delivering team
- the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer who approved the work as fit for its intended use
- the quality assurance sign-off reference from the quality assurance appraisal

## Step 8. Set a review date and approve any new use {#step-8-keep-it-true-after-first-use}

The Analysis Senior Responsible Officer sets a review date with the commissioner, using the cadence
for your level in
[Phase 5, review](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd).

Get the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer to approve any new use before it goes ahead. A new use is
a different purpose, or a change in the context of its use.

Before any reuse, run [the four checks before reuse](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd#check-four-things-before-any-reuse).
If any answer is yes, [score the assurance level again](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).

## Step 9. Review the work and revalidate the designation {#step-9-review-and-revalidate-the-designation}

Revalidate the designation as part of the [Phase 5 review](/guidance/05-review/index.qmd). The
Analysis Senior Responsible Officer does this annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose.

Check it in both directions. Work that was Business Critical may no longer be. Work that was not may
have become so as its use widened.

After sign-off, keep assuring the work:

- Check that it is used as intended, with its caveats.
- Log any errors and record any improvements.
- Keep data and assumptions up to date through scheduled reviews.
- After any material change, review the scope, the specification, the user and technical guides,
  and the quality assurance appraisal and plan, in proportion to the change.
